key_insight: An agent-guided multi-fidelity learning workflow can detect and correct numerical failures in GW-BSE excited-state calculations while preserving the true strain-dependent physics of MoS2-WS2 bilayers.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable, lower-cost prediction of quasiparticle gaps and exciton binding energies for optoelectronic materials workflows relevant to solar cells and other nanoscale semiconductors.
method: Use a structural agent to flag fragile calculations and assign confidence weights.
Select a small set of high-accuracy reference points for calibration.
Apply machine-learning plus Gaussian process corrections to transfer across related systems and quantify uncertainty.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the method corrects spike-like excursions, near-zero-gap collapses, and cross-fidelity inconsistencies, and improves agreement with higher-fidelity references versus a no-agent baseline.
watch_item: The approach still depends on careful identification of numerical fragility, so poor agent screening or limited reference coverage could miss subtle failure modes.
paper_title: Agentic multi-fidelity learning of quasiparticle and excitonic properties
